definitions.explanation: A long, cylindrical yam (Dioscorea polystachya) widely used in Japanese cooking. When grated, it produces a sticky, slimy paste called とろろ, which is eaten over rice or in soups. One of the most common varieties of Japanese yam available in supermarkets.

examples.japanese: {長芋|ながいも}をすりおろす。
{長芋|ながいも}は{生|なま}でも{食|た}べられる。
{長芋|ながいも}を{短冊切|たんざくぎ}りにして{醤油|しょうゆ}と{海苔|のり}で{食|た}べるのが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like cutting nagaimo into strips and eating it with soy sauce and seaweed.

notes:
Compound of {長|なが}い ('long') and {芋|いも} ('yam; potato'). Named for its long, straight shape, which distinguishes it from other varieties of Japanese yam. {長芋|ながいも} is the most readily available and affordable variety of {山芋|やまいも} (mountain yam) in Japanese supermarkets and is a staple ingredient in home cooking.

USAGE:
- When grated, {長芋|ながいも} produces a sticky, mucilaginous paste called とろろ, which is poured over hot rice ({とろろご飯|とろろごはん}) or into soups.
- Can also be sliced into strips ({短冊切|たんざくぎ}り) for salads, or cut into rounds and pan-fried.
- Handling raw {長芋|ながいも} can cause itching on the skin due to needle-like calcium oxalate crystals — a commonly shared kitchen tip.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長芋|ながいも}をすりおろす: to grate nagaimo
- {長芋|ながいも}の{短冊切|たんざくぎ}り: nagaimo cut into strips
- {長芋|ながいも}のとろろ: grated nagaimo paste
- {長芋|ながいも}の{浅漬|あさづ}け: lightly pickled nagaimo

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {山芋|やまいも}: mountain yam — the general category of Japanese yams, of which {長芋|ながいも} is one variety
- {自然薯|じねんじょ}: wild yam — a wild variety that grows naturally in mountainous areas; considered a delicacy with a stronger flavor and stickier texture
- {大和芋|やまといも}: Yamato yam — a flat or hand-shaped variety with a denser, stickier texture than {長芋|ながいも}
